title: Burbank
name: Burbank
metaDescription: 1031 exchange coordination for Burbank Media District office, production-support industrial, and airport-adjacent logistics near Los Angeles.

sections.html: Burbank's commercial real estate runs on its studio campuses and the airport that sits next to them, giving the city a production-and-logistics identity that neighboring Glendale and Hollywood do not share. An exchange buyer identifying a Burbank property is typically choosing among studio-adjacent office, production-support industrial, or airport-area logistics space, and each of the three carries its own tenant pool and re-leasing timeline.

sections.heading: The Media District's Studio-Anchored Office Market
sections.html:
Warner Bros. and Walt Disney Studios anchor Burbank's Media District, and the office buildings surrounding both campuses lease heavily to entertainment, animation, and post-production tenants who value proximity over almost anything else in their site selection. Vacancy and rent trends in this pocket tend to track entertainment-industry hiring and production volume more closely than the broader Los Angeles office market, so a buyer should underwrite that cyclicality directly rather than borrowing assumptions from a downtown or Westside comparable.

A replacement buyer should also separate direct studio leases from the surrounding roster of animation studios, talent agencies, and post-production vendors that lease nearby specifically for proximity rather than any formal studio affiliation. That second group tends to sign shorter terms and carries thinner balance sheets than the major studios themselves, which changes the credit analysis on a Media District rent roll even when a building has no direct studio tenant on it.

sections.heading: Production-Support Industrial Near the Studios
sections.html:
Beyond office towers, Burbank has a real base of production-support industrial space, including scenery and prop fabrication shops, equipment rental warehouses, and post-production facilities that need studio proximity more than highway access. These buildings often carry heavy power and HVAC infrastructure installed for specific production uses, and a replacement buyer should confirm what portion of that build-out transfers value to a new tenant versus what would need to be removed or upgraded.

Clear height and loading configuration matter as much here as in a conventional distribution building, since scenery and prop fabrication tenants move oversized materials in and out on a regular basis, and a building designed for standard office-park loading will not accommodate that use without costly dock and door modifications. A buyer underwriting this niche should walk the loading area with the same attention a distribution-building buyer would give a cross-dock facility.

sections.heading: Airport-Adjacent Logistics and Flex Space
sections.html:
Hollywood Burbank Airport anchors a smaller logistics and flex-space cluster on the city's northern side, serving air-cargo-adjacent tenants and regional distribution uses that value quick access to the airport and the nearby freeways. This inventory behaves more like conventional industrial product than the studio-driven office and production space closer to downtown Burbank, and appraisers should pull comparables accordingly.

Because this cluster is smaller than the industrial markets in the South Bay or along the Long Beach port corridor, a buyer should expect fewer directly comparable sales to draw on when pricing an airport-adjacent Burbank building, and should be prepared to widen the comparable set to nearby Glendale or North Hollywood flex product rather than relying solely on transactions within Burbank's city limits.

sections.heading: The Burbank Identification Set
sections.html:
A realistic Burbank list typically draws from:

  • Media District office buildings near the Warner Bros. and Disney campuses
  • production-support industrial and fabrication space
  • airport-adjacent logistics and flex buildings
  • neighborhood retail serving the surrounding residential population

sections.heading: Sequencing Around Studio and Freeway Access
sections.html:
Because Burbank's value drivers split so clearly between studio proximity and freeway or airport access, a buyer should be explicit about which driver a specific replacement property depends on before finalizing an identification. A qualified intermediary coordinating a Burbank closing should also confirm whether any production-specific infrastructure on an industrial building affects insurance or lender underwriting, since that equipment is not always standard for a generic industrial appraisal.

Buyers often pair a Burbank identification with a Glendale office building or a Van Nuys flex property to keep both underwriting drivers represented on the same three-property list, so that a delay or financing issue tied to specialized production infrastructure on one candidate does not leave the exchange without a workable fallback.

faqs.q: What makes Burbank office demand different from the rest of Los Angeles?
faqs.a: Office demand in the Media District tracks entertainment-industry hiring and production volume closely, since Warner Bros. and Disney anchor the area, so a buyer should underwrite that cyclicality rather than assuming a standard office-market pattern.

faqs.q: Is production-support industrial space common in Burbank?
faqs.a: Yes, and it often includes fabrication shops, equipment rental warehouses, and post-production facilities with heavy power and HVAC build-out installed for specific production uses that may or may not transfer value to a new tenant.

faqs.q: Does the airport affect Burbank's industrial market?
faqs.a: It supports a smaller logistics and flex-space cluster on the city's northern side that behaves more like conventional industrial product than the studio-driven space closer to downtown Burbank.

faqs.q: How does Burbank compare to Hollywood for production-related real estate?
faqs.a: Burbank's studio campuses and surrounding industrial space tend to be larger and more corporate in scale than Hollywood's older, smaller soundstage and support buildings, which also shows up in longer average lease terms among Burbank's anchor studio-adjacent tenants.

faqs.q: What should a buyer confirm before replacing into Burbank industrial space?
faqs.a: Check whether the building carries production-specific power, HVAC, or equipment infrastructure, since that build-out can affect both insurance requirements and how a lender underwrites the asset, and can also change the pool of tenants able to re-lease the space as-is.
